jobs.title: Director, Data Management
jobs.description:
The Director, Data Management will have overall responsibility for the Data Management team, including Clinical Data Managers, Clinical Data Coordinators, Clinical Study Builders and Clinical Data Coders.

The Director, Data Management, will provide strategic leadership and oversight of data management resources, processes, and deliverables, ensuring the quality, integrity, and timely delivery of clinical trial data.

The Director, Data Management will oversee and participate in all clinical data management activities required to ensure that data captured in clinical trials undertaken, or managed by Indero, are collected, managed and reported clearly, accurately and securely. In addition, this position is required to conduct all these activities in conformance with applicable regulatory requirements, industry guidelines and Indero’s SOP while respecting Indero’s commitment to sponsor’s requirements and timelines.

More specifically, the Director, Data Management must:

Strategic Leadership and Collaboration

Inspire, lead and develop all functions within Data Management by helping to formulate a clear vision for the future and attracting and retaining top talent.
Define and drive the Data Management strategy and roadmap, including innovation, standardization and automation initiatives that support the company’s business objectives.
Collaborate with Biostatistics, Risk-Based Study Management, Project Management and other function leaders to align strategies, processes and tools, and to ensure integrated delivery of clinical trial data.
Represent Data Management in sponsor and client meetings and manage the escalation of study risks and issues related to Data Management deliverables.
Monitor industry trends and regulatory changes in clinical data management.
Provide leadership and accountability to study teams assigned to the dedicated client portfolio.

People and Resource Management

Provide direct oversight of data management operations, including planning and assigning work, overseeing the performance of direct reports and conducting performance reviews.
Evaluate the performance of assigned project personnel.
Oversee and provide ongoing training/mentoring to data management and programming staff and review/approve documentation generated by staff, as necessary.
Ensure that all trainings assigned to oneself and to direct and indirect reports are completed on time, and provide direct and indirect reports with appropriate support.
Oversee resource allocation for Data Management activities across clinical trials and internal initiatives.
Lead the development of flexible resourcing strategies, including internal and external resources, to meet the evolving demands of the company.
Adhere to and promote company values and related expected behaviors and follow company SOPs and processes for all deliverables.

Financial Management and Oversight

Oversee budget and resources allocated for Data Management.
Lead the annual Data Management budget planning.
Be responsible for the operational and financial health of Data Management-supported clinical trials by monitoring key operational metrics and supporting budget oversight and forecasting.
Participate in the review of Master Service Agreements (MSA) and work orders with external service providers, process and track payment requests to ensure accordance with the budget and the needs of the study.
Develop Work Orders with external service providers, process and track payment requests to ensure accordance with the budget and the needs of the study.
Oversee activities performed by external service providers to ensure they are done in accordance with effective Work Orders, applicable regulations and Indero SOPs (if applicable).
Oversee the selection, implementation and ongoing management of Data Management systems (e.g., EDC) and strategic technology vendors.

Operational Excellence, Quality and Compliance

Oversee development and optimization of Data Management processes with specific focus on efficiency and quality, while maintaining or exceeding industry best practices.
Define, analyze and monitor Data Management key performance indicators (KPIs) and quality metrics to ensure quality, compliance and timely delivery, and report on performance to senior leadership.
Ensure that Data Management standards, SOPs, processes and trainings are aligned with applicable ICH-GCP guidelines, regulatory authority requirements and industry best practices.
Oversee the definition, writing and updating of data management SOPs.
Monitor timelines and ensure that data management deadlines are met.

Clinical Data Management Delivery

Provide escalation support and expertise to project teams, sponsors and external vendors on complex data management matters, as needed.
Provide support and close oversight to data management team activities for clinical trials from the development of study protocols to the completion of study reports.
Oversee the development of eCRF specifications (including data capture screens and edit check specifications) needed to build a study-specific clinical database/electronic data capture (EDC) system.
Oversee the programming and ongoing maintenance of the clinical database.
Oversee the validation and testing of the clinical database e.g. User Acceptance Testing.
Oversee the development of eCRF completion guidelines and other training material required to train site users and monitors.
Oversee the development of data transfer agreements and specifications with vendors providing external data (e.g. laboratory results).
Oversee the review/development of the data management plan (DMP), and other clinical data management related documentation.
Oversee ongoing data review/cleaning during study conduct.
Ensure that data management documentation is complete and up-to-date in the eTMF.
Oversee the archiving of the clinical database and related documents.

Employee may be assigned to other responsibilities that do not pertain to their former description, if they have the required experience, are qualified and/or have received adequate training.

Requirements:

B.Sc. or M.Sc., or related field;
Minimum of 8 years of leadership experience, plus at least 15 years of clinical trials experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical or CRO industry.
Proven experience leading and developing data management teams and managing multiple studies and sponsor portfolios.
Demonstrated experience leading global or cross-functional initiatives and influencing strategy across multiple stakeholders.
Experience with budget planning and resource management, including the oversight of external vendors.
Experience in the setup, validation and oversight of EDC systems and other clinical data systems.
Experience supporting sponsor audits and regulatory inspections is an asset.
Strong knowledge of ICH-GCP, CDISC standards (CDASH, SDTM), and applicable data protection regulations.
Strategic thinking, with the ability to define a vision and translate it into operational plans.
Strong leadership and coaching skills, with the ability to teach, train and mentor employees at all levels.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence at all levels of the organization and with external stakeholders in a matrix, cross-functional environment.
Strong organizational and planning skills, with the ability to prioritize multiple competing demands in a fast-paced environment.
Sound judgment, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; French is an asset.
Good knowledge of good clinical practices, and applicable Health Canada and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations/guidelines.

Our company:

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

Permanent full-time position
Flexible schedule
Vacation
Home-based position
Ongoing learning and development

A Global Clinical Leader In Dermatology!

﻿Formerly known as Innovaderm, Indero is a world-renowned expert and clinical research leader in dermatology. We have more than two decades of experience serving a broad range of indications, patient populations, administration routes, and drug classes, and a global footprint.

﻿Indero is a dual-focus CRO for dermatology and rheumatology, with 25+ years’ experience in clinical research and trial delivery. Our full-service approach – which includes everything from protocol design and patient recruitment to trial monitoring and biometrics – provides biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors with the rigorous scientific foundation and tailored expertise their studies need to reach the finish line efficiently and effectively. With capabilities in North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and Latin America; vast, continuously growing relationships with investigators and patients; and a dedicated research clinic through which we design and execute our own studies, Indero is the ideal CRO partner for clinical needs at global scale.

About Charitable Impact

Charitable Impact started as a bold idea and evolved quickly into an unwavering belief: everyone should have access to resources that help them build the brighter future they imagine. We provide a donor-centric giving platform, supported by a donor advised fund, that helps people amplify their generosity to create the change they want to see in the world. Anyone can use it to find and give to their favourite charities from one place, give with friends and others, and get support with making their biggest impact possible. So far, Canadians across the country have donated more than $1.6 billion through our platform. 

We take care of each other

Our team members enjoy competitive salaries, purposeful perks, and a culture that gives back and has fun doing it. We're proud to have been named one of Canada’s Most Admired™ Corporate Cultures of 2024 and winner of the Gamechanger: Company Culture Award at BC Tech's 2026 Technology Impact Awards. We support each other, learn from one another, and grow together. We're on an adventure to make giving an intentional and meaningful part of daily life. So, come and join us, and let's build a brighter future together.

What you’ll do

The Head of Product is a high-impact leadership role with broad influence across Charitable Impact. Leading both Product Management and UX, and reporting to the VP, Experience & Growth, this role sits at the intersection of product vision, organizational priorities, and execution. Working closely with our founder, who plays a central role in shaping product direction, the Head of Product is responsible for understanding that vision deeply, translating it into clear priorities, and creating the conditions for teams to carry it forward with focus and coherence.

A major part of the role is orchestration across our seven product streams. The Head of Product maintains a clear view of how the different parts of the product fit together: where work intersects, where dependencies exist, where sequencing matters, and where trade-offs need to be made. You help ensure individual streams do not operate as isolated bodies of work, but contribute to a connected product direction and a consistent experience for our users.

The role is accountable for the effectiveness and output of both Product Management and UX teams. You'll maintain a clear and ongoing view of product health, using data, experimentation, and performance measures to understand what's working, where the product is underperforming, and where teams should focus next.

You'll work closely with Engineering, Marketing, Donor Engagement & Experience, Business Development, Data, and the broader Leadership team to connect product decisions with the needs and priorities of the organization. This is a role for an experienced product practitioner who is also willing to deeply learn the context of our product: what makes it unique, the charity context in which it exists, its history, strengths, constraints, dependencies, and opportunities - and use that understanding to guide teams as Charitable Impact continues to evolve and mature its product practice.

We're a hybrid office and this role requires PCT availability and in-office attendance once per quarter in our Vancouver office. This role will lead distributed teams across Canada and India and will require time-zone flexibility (early morning/evenings PCT).

Your responsibilities

Product Strategy & Portfolio Leadership

Work closely with our founder to translate product vision and strategic direction into clear priorities, roadmaps, and executable plans.
Maintain a coherent portfolio view across all seven product streams, including sequencing, dependencies, trade-offs, and performance measurement. 
Lead quarterly product planning and help translate company priorities into clear product and experience OKRs.
Ensure related work across streams is coordinated rather than developed in isolation.
Represent Product and UX in leadership forums and company-wide planning.

Product + UX Leadership

Lead Product Management and User Experience as an integrated product-development function.
Inspire and mentor the team, creating a collaborative and inclusive culture.
Develop a culture of creativity, innovation, and continuous improvement within the team.
Lead by example, demonstrating a relentless commitment to excellence.
Develop annual and quarterly departmental plans and objectives.
Cultivate a strong sense of ownership and accountability within the team, empowering team members to take initiative and drive projects forward.
Foster strong cross-functional partnerships with other teams and stakeholders to align departmental efforts with company goals and objectives.
Continue to support our environment of care and compassion for one-another, and nurture our culture that values considerate and empathetic collaboration.

Product Performance, Data & Experimentation

Establish a clear framework for product performance, including activation, adoption, engagement, retention, conversion, and feature usage.

Build stronger connections between product strategy, behavioural data, UX research, and user insight.

Continuous learning and paid professional development opportunities
A creative, welcoming culture committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion

The Director, Data Management will have overall responsibility for the Data Management team, including Clinical Data Managers, Clinical Data Coordinators, Clinical Study Builders and Clinical Data Coders.

The Director, Data Management, will provide strategic leadership and oversight of data management resources, processes, and deliverables, ensuring the quality, integrity, and timely delivery of clinical trial data.

The Director, Data Management will oversee and participate in all clinical data management activities required to ensure that data captured in clinical trials undertaken, or managed by Indero, are collected, managed and reported clearly, accurately and securely. In addition, this position is required to conduct all these activities in conformance with applicable regulatory requirements, industry guidelines and Indero’s SOP while respecting Indero’s commitment to sponsor’s requirements and timelines.

More specifically, the Director, Data Management must:

Strategic Leadership and Collaboration

Inspire, lead and develop all functions within Data Management by helping to formulate a clear vision for the future and attracting and retaining top talent.
Define and drive the Data Management strategy and roadmap, including innovation, standardization and automation initiatives that support the company’s business objectives.
Collaborate with Biostatistics, Risk-Based Study Management, Project Management and other function leaders to align strategies, processes and tools, and to ensure integrated delivery of clinical trial data.
Represent Data Management in sponsor and client meetings and manage the escalation of study risks and issues related to Data Management deliverables.
Monitor industry trends and regulatory changes in clinical data management.
Provide leadership and accountability to study teams assigned to the dedicated client portfolio.

People and Resource Management

Provide direct oversight of data management operations, including planning and assigning work, overseeing the performance of direct reports and conducting performance reviews.
Evaluate the performance of assigned project personnel.
Oversee and provide ongoing training/mentoring to data management and programming staff and review/approve documentation generated by staff, as necessary.
Ensure that all trainings assigned to oneself and to direct and indirect reports are completed on time, and provide direct and indirect reports with appropriate support.
Oversee resource allocation for Data Management activities across clinical trials and internal initiatives.
Lead the development of flexible resourcing strategies, including internal and external resources, to meet the evolving demands of the company.
Adhere to and promote company values and related expected behaviors and follow company SOPs and processes for all deliverables.

Financial Management and Oversight

Oversee budget and resources allocated for Data Management.
Lead the annual Data Management budget planning.
Be responsible for the operational and financial health of Data Management-supported clinical trials by monitoring key operational metrics and supporting budget oversight and forecasting.
Participate in the review of Master Service Agreements (MSA) and work orders with external service providers, process and track payment requests to ensure accordance with the budget and the needs of the study.
Develop Work Orders with external service providers, process and track payment requests to ensure accordance with the budget and the needs of the study.
Oversee activities performed by external service providers to ensure they are done in accordance with effective Work Orders, applicable regulations and Indero SOPs (if applicable).
Oversee the selection, implementation and ongoing management of Data Management systems (e.g., EDC) and strategic technology vendors.

Operational Excellence, Quality and Compliance

Oversee development and optimization of Data Management processes with specific focus on efficiency and quality, while maintaining or exceeding industry best practices.
Define, analyze and monitor Data Management key performance indicators (KPIs) and quality metrics to ensure quality, compliance and timely delivery, and report on performance to senior leadership.
Ensure that Data Management standards, SOPs, processes and trainings are aligned with applicable ICH-GCP guidelines, regulatory authority requirements and industry best practices.
Oversee the definition, writing and updating of data management SOPs.
Monitor timelines and ensure that data management deadlines are met.

Clinical Data Management Delivery

Provide escalation support and expertise to project teams, sponsors and external vendors on complex data management matters, as needed.
Provide support and close oversight to data management team activities for clinical trials from the development of study protocols to the completion of study reports.
Oversee the development of eCRF specifications (including data capture screens and edit check specifications) needed to build a study-specific clinical database/electronic data capture (EDC) system.
Oversee the programming and ongoing maintenance of the clinical database.
Oversee the validation and testing of the clinical database e.g. User Acceptance Testing.
Oversee the development of eCRF completion guidelines and other training material required to train site users and monitors.
Oversee the development of data transfer agreements and specifications with vendors providing external data (e.g. laboratory results).
Oversee the review/development of the data management plan (DMP), and other clinical data management related documentation.
Oversee ongoing data review/cleaning during study conduct.
Ensure that data management documentation is complete and up-to-date in the eTMF.
Oversee the archiving of the clinical database and related documents.

Employee may be assigned to other responsibilities that do not pertain to their former description, if they have the required experience, are qualified and/or have received adequate training.

Requirements:

B.Sc. or M.Sc., or related field;
Minimum of 8 years of leadership experience, plus at least 15 years of clinical trials experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical or CRO industry.
Proven experience leading and developing data management teams and managing multiple studies and sponsor portfolios.
Demonstrated experience leading global or cross-functional initiatives and influencing strategy across multiple stakeholders.
Experience with budget planning and resource management, including the oversight of external vendors.
Experience in the setup, validation and oversight of EDC systems and other clinical data systems.
Experience supporting sponsor audits and regulatory inspections is an asset.
Strong knowledge of ICH-GCP, CDISC standards (CDASH, SDTM), and applicable data protection regulations.
Strategic thinking, with the ability to define a vision and translate it into operational plans.
Strong leadership and coaching skills, with the ability to teach, train and mentor employees at all levels.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence at all levels of the organization and with external stakeholders in a matrix, cross-functional environment.
Strong organizational and planning skills, with the ability to prioritize multiple competing demands in a fast-paced environment.
Sound judgment, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; French is an asset.
Good knowledge of good clinical practices, and applicable Health Canada and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations/guidelines.

Our company:

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

Permanent full-time position
Flexible schedule
Vacation
Home-based position
Ongoing learning and development

A Global Clinical Leader In Dermatology!

﻿Formerly known as Innovaderm, Indero is a world-renowned expert and clinical research leader in dermatology. We have more than two decades of experience serving a broad range of indications, patient populations, administration routes, and drug classes, and a global footprint.

- Define the company’s service management strategy, annual operational goals, and execution plans.
- Develop a service operations management framework aligned with the company’s business growth.
- Establish service management policies, service standards, and operational guidelines.
- Optimize the service organizational structure and operational management model.
- Enhance the scalability and long-term operational sustainability of the service ecosystem.

- Analyze issues arising during service delivery and drive root-cause remediation.
- Streamline service processes to reduce redundant tasks and operational delays.

- Monitor compliance with Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
- Track key metrics such as service response times, resolution times, and completion rates.
- Maintain service operations dashboards and management reporting systems.

V. Resource and Capacity Management

- Continuously enhance customer service standards and the overall service experience.

- Identify opportunities for cost optimization and drive improvement initiatives.

We support each other, learn from one another, and grow together. We're on an adventure to make giving an intentional and meaningful part of daily life. So, come and join us, and let's build a brighter future together.

What you’ll do

The Head of Product is a high-impact leadership role with broad influence across Charitable Impact. Leading both Product Management and UX, and reporting to the VP, Experience & Growth, this role sits at the intersection of product vision, organizational priorities, and execution. Working closely with our founder, who plays a central role in shaping product direction, the Head of Product is responsible for understanding that vision deeply, translating it into clear priorities, and creating the conditions for teams to carry it forward with focus and coherence.

A major part of the role is orchestration across our seven product streams. The Head of Product maintains a clear view of how the different parts of the product fit together: where work intersects, where dependencies exist, where sequencing matters, and where trade-offs need to be made. You help ensure individual streams do not operate as isolated bodies of work, but contribute to a connected product direction and a consistent experience for our users.

The role is accountable for the effectiveness and output of both Product Management and UX teams. You'll maintain a clear and ongoing view of product health, using data, experimentation, and performance measures to understand what's working, where the product is underperforming, and where teams should focus next.

You'll work closely with Engineering, Marketing, Donor Engagement & Experience, Business Development, Data, and the broader Leadership team to connect product decisions with the needs and priorities of the organization. This is a role for an experienced product practitioner who is also willing to deeply learn the context of our product: what makes it unique, the charity context in which it exists, its history, strengths, constraints, dependencies, and opportunities - and use that understanding to guide teams as Charitable Impact continues to evolve and mature its product practice.

We're a hybrid office and this role requires PCT availability and in-office attendance once per quarter in our Vancouver office. This role will lead distributed teams across Canada and India and will require time-zone flexibility (early morning/evenings PCT).

Your responsibilities

Product Strategy & Portfolio Leadership

Work closely with our founder to translate product vision and strategic direction into clear priorities, roadmaps, and executable plans.
Maintain a coherent portfolio view across all seven product streams, including sequencing, dependencies, trade-offs, and performance measurement. 
Lead quarterly product planning and help translate company priorities into clear product and experience OKRs.
Ensure related work across streams is coordinated rather than developed in isolation.
Represent Product and UX in leadership forums and company-wide planning.

Lead Product Management and User Experience as an integrated product-development function.
Inspire and mentor the team, creating a collaborative and inclusive culture.
Develop a culture of creativity, innovation, and continuous improvement within the team.
Lead by example, demonstrating a relentless commitment to excellence.
Develop annual and quarterly departmental plans and objectives.
Cultivate a strong sense of ownership and accountability within the team, empowering team members to take initiative and drive projects forward.
Foster strong cross-functional partnerships with other teams and stakeholders to align departmental efforts with company goals and objectives.
Continue to support our environment of care and compassion for one-another, and nurture our culture that values considerate and empathetic collaboration.

Establish a clear framework for product performance, including activation, adoption, engagement, retention, conversion, and feature usage.
Ensure major product initiatives have clear success measures and appropriate instrumentation before release.
Build stronger connections between product strategy, behavioural data, UX research, and user insight.
Establish a regular cadence for reviewing product performance and identifying where iteration is needed.
Build A/B testing and controlled experimentation into product development where appropriate.
Help teams translate assumptions into testable hypotheses, measurable outcomes, and evidence-based decisions.
Partner with Engineering and Data to improve the quality, accessibility, and reliability of product analytics.

Partner with Engineering leadership to calibrate realistic delivery expectations based on capacity, complexity and dependencies.

Product strategy is translated into a coherent portfolio of work across the seven streams.

PM and UX function as a unified unit with greater effective capacity.

new_jobs.description:
Flow Capital is a publicly listed provider of flexible growth capital for high-growth technology and tech-enabled companies. We specialize in founder-friendly, minimally dilutive venture debt, providing $1 million to $15 million in financing to revenue-generating businesses across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. We work with both VC-backed and founder-owned companies seeking capital to accelerate growth, extend runway, or fund strategic initiatives without the significant dilution. Since inception, Flow Capital has invested over $185 million across over 75 companies.

Our rapid growth requires the addition of a Associate Director or Director
to join our the investment origination team. The job is located in Toronto, Canada. Exceptional candidates working remotely within Canada will be considered. 

How you will contribute:

Meet with prospective borrowers
Read/review business plans and pitch decks
Gather industry information for prospective investments, including research into potential competitors to target companies
Review financial materials provided by prospective borrowers and prepare follow up questions for further meetings
Structure and negotiate term sheets with prospective borrowers
Assist with preparing internal investment memorandums
Maintain and support internal databases and tools
Build a network of prospective deal referral partners including venture capital firms, investment bankers, debt advisors and others
Attend conferences and networking events
Contribute to the ongoing development of our marketing strategy

Qualifications
:
6-12 years’ of relevant direct experience or in related fields (venture debt, venture capital, commercial banking, corporate finance, private investments, or equity research)
Demonstrated experience reviewing a high volume of transactions as an investor or advisor
Demonstrated sales or origination experience required
Demonstrated experience structuring and negotiating financing transactions
Solid understanding of corporate finance and accounting principles, including proficiency with financial modeling and valuation techniques
An relevant degree with academic coursework in finance, economics, or accounting and an outstanding academic achievement.
Exceptional verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills
Outstanding analytical skills with high attention to detail
Proactive, highly motivated, and with strong aptitude to work independently 
Passionate for uncovering the most compelling risk adjusted investment opportunities
Be comfortable working in a fast-paced, high-expectation environment 
Experience in the technology sector or in dealing with revenue stage, small and medium-sized, high-growth companies
Completion the CFA or CPA programs is an asset
A wide network within the venture ecosystem in Canada and the US is an asset

Flow Capital, an equal opportunity employer, offers a strong compensation package for the right candidate and the opportunity to work in a highly entrepreneurial, fast-paced environment. new_jobs.description:
Position: Executive Director
Employment Type: Part-Time (20 hours/week), Independent Contractor
Compensation: Commensurate with experience and qualifications
Reports To: Board of Directors
Location: Work from Home

Must be available to travel to meetings across the counties we serve. Preference to individuals living in one of the regions we serve or within 50 km of any of the regions we serve (eg. Oxford, London, Middlesex, Huron-Perth, Grey-Bruce). 

Must be eligible to work in Canada, and hold a class G drivers licence. 
The successful candidate will be asked to complete an OPP record check, including a vulnerable sector screening. 

Deadline to Apply: 

Applications will be reviewed and assessed on an ongoing basis until the position has been filled. 
Please submit a cover letter and resume to: info@facilefutures.ca and include the Subjectline “Application to Facile Executive Director Position” 

About Facile Futures

At Facile Futures, we believe everyone deserves to live a meaningful, connected, and self-directed life. As a family-founded and family-led organization, we recognize individuals and families as experts in their own lives, with unique strengths, experiences, and aspirations.
Through relationships, collaboration, and person-directed approaches, we work alongside people and families to navigate challenges, strengthen connections, and create opportunities for belonging, inclusion, and possibility. Our work is grounded in dignity, self-determination, equity, and the belief that stronger communities are built when people are heard, valued, and empowered.

The Opportunity

This is an exciting time for Facile! After three years of growth and expansion, we’re looking for the right leader to take our organization forward. Facile Futures is seeking a compassionate, collaborative, and values-driven Executive Director to lead organizational operations while working alongside individuals and families. With a 15 year history of walking alongside people with a disability and their families, we are a trusted source for planning and facilitation. Families depend on us for creative solutions, innovation leadership and strategic advocacy. Balancing nonprofit administration with relationship-based family support, the Executive Director will collaborate with the Board, staff, families, and community partners to strengthen sustainability, advance inclusion, and create meaningful opportunities for growth and connection.

What's in it for You?

Flexible, self-directed schedule and work-from-home arrangement
Purposeful work supporting family-led, community-driven initiatives
Continuous learning and paid professional development opportunities
A creative, welcoming culture committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion

Key Responsibilities

Person-Directed and Family-Focused Leadership
Build trusting, respectful relationships with individuals and families, honouring their unique experiences, choices, and aspirations
Lead and mentor a team of facilitators supporting person-directed planning, self-determination, and supported decision-making
Create opportunities for families to connect, share experiences, and strengthen supportive networks
Ensure people with a disability and their families have a meaningful influence on organizational priorities, programs, and decisions
Respond to emerging needs with empathy, creativity, and collaborative problem-solving
Strengthen connections to community resources and services without imposing predetermined definitions of success

Organizational Leadership and Operations
Lead day-to-day operations, ensuring effective administration, organizational accountability, and alignment with Facile Futures' mission
Collaborate with the Board to implement strategic priorities, establish measurable goals, and identify opportunities for innovation and growth
Develop and maintain organizational policies, procedures, systems, and records
Oversee budgets, expenditures, financial reporting, and coordination with accounting supports
Ensure compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, funding, and reporting requirements
Supervise and support team members and volunteers, fostering a culture of trust, inclusion, accountability, and continuous learning
Manage organizational priorities and resources effectively within a part-time leadership structure

Community Partnerships and Advocacy
Develop relationships with community organizations, service providers, school boards, funders, and Ministry stakeholders
Represent Facile Futures in community networks, partnerships, and collaborative initiatives
Support families in navigating systems and accessing opportunities aligned with their goals
Advocate for inclusive, equitable, and person-directed approaches that reflect the voices and priorities of people with disabilities and their families
Identify opportunities to strengthen community capacity, accessibility, and meaningful participation

Fund Development and Sustainability
Collaborate with the Board to strengthen financial sustainability through funding, partnerships, and entrepreneurial opportunities
Develop grant applications, funding proposals, and fundraising initiatives
Cultivate relationships with funders, donors, and community supporters
Explore diversified revenue opportunities that support Facile Futures' independence and unencumbered service status
Communicate organizational impact through meaningful outcomes and stories that respect individual dignity, privacy, and consent

Board Relations and Governance
Maintain a transparent, collaborative, and accountable relationship with the Board of Directors
Provide timely operational updates, financial information, and strategic recommendations
Support Board meetings, annual reporting, recruitment, and governance activities
Respect the distinction between governance and operational leadership while encouraging shared learning and thoughtful decision-making

Who We're Looking For

We recognize that effective leadership develops through diverse professional, personal, and community experiences. Candidates may bring backgrounds in nonprofit leadership, entrepreneurship, disability advocacy, family support, community development, or related fields.

Values and Leadership Approach
Strong commitment to person-directed, co-creative, and family-led practices, equity, inclusion, and self-determination
Ability to listen deeply, build authentic relationships, and respect the expertise of individuals and families
Compassionate, collaborative, and ethical leadership grounded in trust, transparency, and accountability
Creativity, adaptability, initiative, and an entrepreneurial approach to problem-solving and organizational growth

Experience and Skills
Experience in nonprofit management, entrepreneurship, community programming, family support, advocacy, or a related field
Strong administrative, financial management, organizational, and communication skills
Experience collaborating with families, community partners, and diverse stakeholders
Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and lead within a part-time role
Experience in strategic planning, project management, fundraising and grant writing is essential. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in written and spoken English. Language proficiency may be assessed as part of the recruitment process.
Knowledge of disability services and systems (e.g., DSO, ODSP), person-directed planning, and community inclusion is an asset
Experience working with a volunteer Board of Directors is an asset

We value lived experience. People with disabilities, family members, caregivers, and others with relevant lived experience are encouraged to apply. Formal education may be an asset, but we welcome candidates whose skills, knowledge, and leadership abilities have developed through diverse pathways.

Working Arrangements and Compensation

This is a part-time, independent contractor position (20 hours per week) offering flexible scheduling and a work-from-home arrangement. The role combines organizational administration, strategic leadership, and meaningful engagement with individuals, families, and community partners.
Compensation will reflect the successful candidate's experience, qualifications, and agreed-upon responsibilities.
